item.title: Cornell’s President Acknowledges Missteps in Handling of Rape Accusations
item.description: In an interview with The New York Times, Michael Kotlikoff addressed his administration’s handling of sexual assault accusations brought by a former student.
item.dc:creator: Debra Kamin
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michael Kotlikoff moved from his interim role to a permanent position as president of Cornell in October 2025.

item.title: The Controversial Class That M.I.T. Is Paying a Professor Not to Teach
item.description: Michel DeGraff, a vocal pro-Palestinian activist, can’t be easily fired because he has tenure. But he has been kicked out of his department.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michel DeGraff, a tenured professor at M.I.T., was pushed out of the university’s linguistics section.

item.title: Cornell Bans Fraternity Parties and Adds Sexual Assault Investigators
item.description: The expansive changes to campus life, including working closely with the state police, come in the wake of the national uproar caused by allegations of a gang rape at a fraternity house.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman and Debra Kamin
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: Posters left over from a rally over a student’s sexual assault allegations are displayed in the windows of Milstein Hall at Cornell University.

item.title: France’s Long, Fervent History of Protest
item.description: Student demonstrations in recent weeks re-lit a centuries-old torch of civil resistance. How do they compare to previous movements in France?
item.dc:creator: Zane Irwin
item.media:description: A student attacking the police in Paris during the May 1968 student uprising.

item.title: He Left Behind Millions. Who Would Get It — His Family, or the D.S.A.?
item.description: When a New York University professor died in 2024, it set off a legal dispute over a quietly accumulated fortune.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Weiser
item.media:description: David Greenberg, a longtime sociology professor at New York University, died in 2024. He left behind more than just a legacy of writing and teaching.

item.title: How Cornell University Chi Phi Fraternity Members Responded After Rape Accusation
item.description: Records reveal how fraternity members responded when a fellow student accused them of sexual assault.
item.dc:creator: Michael Wilson
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: A former Cornell University student filed a lawsuit saying she was sexually assaulted by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity at a house party on campus.

item.title: At Cornell, a Sorority Finds Itself Sued by One of Its Own
item.description: Some Delta Delta Delta members are asking if the sorority shares blame in the bombshell case — or if the group is a scapegoat.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman and Andrea Barnes
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell chapter of the Delta Delta Delta sorority found itself a defendant in a civil suit by one of its members.

item.title: Princeton Celebrates Anne Carson, a Nobel Prize Winner Who Was Denied Tenure
item.description: Carson, who was awarded the Literature prize on Thursday, was denied tenure when teaching at the university in the 1980s, leading social media users to mock a congratulatory message.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:credit: Pontus Lundahl/TT News Agency, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson in 2015. She left the faculty of Princeton University in the mid-1980s after she was denied tenure.

item.title: Hochul Opts New York Into Trump-Backed School Voucher Plan
item.description: The governor’s decision, which is at odds with New York’s teachers’ unions, would provide federal tax dollars to parents for both private and public school expenses.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haag
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Kathy Hochul agreed to opt into a federal tax credit program open to private and public school parents.

item.title: Man Threatened After Wrong Address Mix-Up in Cornell Lawsuit
item.description: The lawyer for Jane Doe said his team identified the wrong person and apologized for the error. Now, the judge in the case has ordered sensitive information to be sealed.
item.dc:creator: Santul Nerkar and Troy Closson
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: The wrong man was served in the Cornell sexual assault lawsuit, and his address remained on a public docket, which led to him and his family receiving threats and harassment.

item.title: Book Review: ‘The Best Kind of American,’ by Kim Ghattas
item.description: In “The Best Kind of American,” Kim Ghattas shows what an American’s assassination in Lebanon four decades ago reveals about chaos in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Christopher de Bellaigue
item.category: The Best Kind of American: A True Story of Murder, War, and America's Undoing in the Middle East (Book)

item.title: Trump Administration Suspends Microsoft From Green Card Program, Alleging Visa Fraud
item.description: Vice President JD Vance singled out the tech firm as he and other officials accused an array of companies and universities of abusing the visa system.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” Vice President JD Vance said in Washington on Thursday.

item.title: After Week of Turmoil at Cornell, a Heavy Cloud Hangs Over Student Life
item.description: As the weekend arrived, much of the nightlife in the upstate New York college town was subdued. But there were still some students looking to cut loose.
item.dc:creator: Maia Coleman
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: Students and patrons outside bars and restaurants on Friday night in Ithaca, N.Y., home to Cornell. Many said they couldn’t remember a weekend on campus this quiet.

item.title: A Campus Reckoning: ‘Cornell Is Now Known for This’
item.description: Accusations of sexual assault at a fraternity party have tarnished the self-image of a fiercely proud Ivy League institution. Can the university ever be the same?
item.dc:creator: John Leland and Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: On the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., the rituals of a new school year have been replaced with a reassessment of what it means to be a student there.

item.title: Cornell’s President Grilled by Faculty Senate Over Handling of Crisis
item.description: Ahead of a vote on a resolution of no confidence in Michael I. Kotlikoff, some faculty members said they were not swayed by steps he announced on Tuesday, including banning fraternity parties.

item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: Faculty, students and staff members at Cornell University attended a meeting of the faculty senate on Wednesday to consider the role of the university president.

item.title: The Crisis Playbook for Universities in Trouble

item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: In comments this week, Cornell’s president, Michael I. Kotlikoff, acknowledged anger and “a loss of trust” in Cornell’s leadership.
